about: The painted backdrop beyond the walkable area of S3, the Rainbow Bridge (rainbow_bridge, scan u 15500-20500) (map/BUILDING.md: painting, not models). tools/backdrop.mjs restyles each panel from the scroll strip that lies past that edge (scan rect u0,v0,u1,v1) with prompts/backdrop_panel.txt + the panel's content prompt (prompts/backdrop_rainbow_bridge_<side>.txt): seen at eye level on plain white, which ship keys out with clean edges; it measures the painted horizon, and web/src/backdrop.js stands the panel on the ring (angles: 0 = east, 90 = north, 180 = west) at its true aspect with that horizon at eye level, its foot in ground mist. Everything outside the painted area is veiled in mist (the scroll's blank silk). West is S4 part 2 (outer_road_2, u 12600-15500) and east is S2 (canal, from u 20500): with streaming a panel stands in whenever that neighbour isn't loaded (S3 alone, ?window=0, or before the neighbour is built) and drops by itself when it is. North: the silk's top edge cuts the far bank's shops, the north bank's buildings and the willows' crowns, and nothing is painted beyond them, so mist only. South (below the silk's bottom edge): mist only; the river where it leaves the silk: mist.

panels.why: S4 part 2 (outer_road_2, u 12600-15500) lies past the west seam: its whole strip, from the moorings with the five rafted boats, the old willow and the tea house at the seam, past the wheelwright's yard and the pack mules on the top street, to the crowd round the seated man, the two palm-covered carts and the office hall at S4 part 1's seam. The seam leans with the scroll's receding direction (dx 31.6 at u 15500), so from S3's centre (121.38, 13.07; the mean of painted_area's corners) it spans 156.3 deg (nw, 81.65/30.54, 43.4 m) to 214.5 deg (sw, 95.98/-4.39, 30.8 m): the panel is centred on 185 and as wide (58), its right (north) end over the river and the far bank, its left (south) end over the south row's halls. On S4b's layout the strip's things lie from the centre at: the moored boats 151-175 deg (36-42 m), the tea house 185 (44 m), the south halls 197-208 (33-49 m), the wheelwright 179 (54 m), the palm carts 186-193 (59-64 m), the crowd's shop 172 (67 m): every one inside the panel's span and within the 70 m ring, so the strip is the whole of S4b and nothing beyond it.
panels.picked: 2026-10-12, by the S3 backdrop agent. Candidates 0-1 are draw 2 (gen/sections/rainbow_bridge/backdrop/draw2_2026-10-12, the content prompt as it is now), 2-3 are draw 1 (draw1_2026-10-12, its first content prompt kept there as content_prompt_west.txt). Measured each (ship --review): ground strip 0.0332 / 0.0527 / 0.0430 / 0.0586 of the width, near-white 2.6 / 3.5 / 4.4 / 4.6%. Draw 1's best (2) put a big open hall full of diners on the road's left, the south, where the strip paints only the backs of the south row's halls, so the tea house stood on the wrong side, and it had no wheelwright's yard, no sedan chair and one palm cart; draw 2's prompt said the left holds only plain back walls and heavy roofs with nobody sitting, put the tea house right of the middle, and named the wheelwright's wheel, the two carts and the sedan chair firmly. Picked 0 (ground strip 0.0332: on its own 70 m circle the page needs no lift, its horizon stands at the eye, the first street panel to do so; near-white 2.6%; 156 KB webp, 172 KB KTX2). It holds the strip's things in their places in the viewer's frame: on the left of the road the long white back walls and heavy grey roofs of the south row's halls, one behind another, straw heaps along their backs; on the road a palm-thatched cart coming toward us behind a light ox with its driver, the saddled dark horse with two men and a small donkey, the second palm cart parked far off; on the right the tea house (open hall, grey gable roof, mat canopy, men at tables) under a pollard willow with a fan of stiff shoots, the big bare elm with crooked twigs, the wheelwright's yard (the wheel lying flat, a man bending over it, the hooped pole frame, timbers and poles), the open ground climbing to the top street with four pack animals and the long row of open eating houses, a tall straight bare trunk among bare trees; nearest on the right the five boats moored side by side at the bank (two cabin boats, three under barrel mat roofs) and, small at the right end, the cabin boat by the far bank; low tiled houses and bare trees along the far bank. Its departures: two willows behind the south halls hang thin pale strands (a weeping shape, sparse and leafless; the scroll's seam willow by the south roofs does hang whips between its leaders, but its crown fans); the south halls show small open fronts with mat awnings and a few people under their eaves; the road runs on between rows of halls to a vanishing point; no crowd round the seated man, no sedan chair that reads; a small open shed at the left end; the old seam willow with its long level limb is not there (the tea house's pollard stands in its place). Rejected: 1 (draw 2) has correct pollards and the crowd before the shops, the round parasol and the two tall elms, but three palm carts, the road as a long avenue of identical houses to the horizon, and ground strip 0.0527 (the page would lift it); 2 (draw 1) as above, the tea house on the south side; 3 (draw 1) paints weeping willows with green hanging strands, long shop rows on both sides running to a vanishing point, the road as a deep wedge (0.0586).

panels.why: S2 (canal, from u 20500) lies past the east seam. The seam leans (dx 30.4 at u 20500), so from S3's centre (121.38, 13.07) it spans -23.9 deg (se, 160.85/-4.39, 43.2 m) to 34.2 deg (ne, 147.06/30.54, 31.1 m): the panel is centred on 5 and as wide (58), its left (north) end over the north bank's shops, its right (south) end over the south bank's hall. Looking east the strip's u runs away from us, so its length sets how far down the river the view reaches. On S2's layout the 70 m ring crosses S2 at about u 23300-24300 (the moored boats at the seam 33-39 m from the centre, the sweep boat 53 m, the passenger boat 63 m, the dining terrace 61 m, the mat-roofed boat 67 m, the mule cart 73 m, the hooded cargo boat 80 m, the towed boat 82 m). The strip ends at u 24300, a little past the lead's 23000-24000, so that the trackers' one tow line (they walk at u 21870-22170) ends at the masthead of the boat it tows (逆水行舟, mast at u 24183, at 357 deg, the panel's middle), and the two big boats there close the view down the river as the bridge closes S4b's east panel; it cuts the mule cart (u 24305) at its middle, a small far thing at the panel's left. Everything from the seam to there lies inside the panel's span: the north bank 8-18 deg, the river's boats 357-2 deg, the south bank 340-348 deg.
panels.picked: 2026-10-12, by the S3 backdrop agent. Candidates 0-1 are draw 2 (gen/sections/rainbow_bridge/backdrop/draw2_2026-10-12, the content prompt as it is now), 2-3 are draw 1 (draw1_2026-10-12, its first content prompt kept there as content_prompt_east.txt). Measured each (ship --review): ground strip 0.0762 / 0.1094 / 0.0781 / 0.0625 of the width, near-white 10.2 / 9.0 / 10.8 / 7.2%. Every candidate paints the river as a channel running away to a vanishing point. Picked 2 (draw 1's first; ground strip 0.0781, the page lifts it 1.3 m, horizon 1.1 deg over the eye on its own 70 m circle; near-white 10.8%; 312 KB webp, 279 KB KTX2). It keeps the strip's order from near to far: on the left (north bank) the two pollard willows by a tall slat fence, the shop row with open bays and people, the boats moored with their bows toward us (a cargo boat under an arched mat roof with its crew, one fending off with a pole, a mat-roofed boat, a cabin boat with its steersman), the file of trackers on the bank hauling a line, the white plastered wall with its gateway door, the willow with a forked trunk, the long house with its band of lattice windows, the dining terrace on posts with its balustrade, diners and a gabled pavilion; in the middle the boat with six men crowded at its stern coming toward us and, farthest, the big boat with one tall mast and its stays, a tow line from its bow; on the right (south bank) a leaning dark-trunked pollard, the huge forked pollard, the small canopy boat with a man in it and people on the bank handing something to him, an open boat, a long mat-roofed boat, the thatched building and the house with an open gable truss. Every willow is a pollard with a fan of stiff bare shoots, none weeps. Its departures: the river runs on past the masted boat to the horizon between rows of houses on both banks (S2 paints more river and north-bank shops beyond u 24300, but no south bank there); the very long passenger boat under the terrace and the hooded cargo boat beside the masted boat are missing; about seven trackers and a knot of bent figures by the moored boats instead of five; the towed boat's line runs from its bow; a paved edge along the south bank; its pollards' pale buds read slightly frosted at night (10.8%, as S4b's shipped east panel's 10.3%). Rejected: 0 (draw 2) puts the far eatery, the porters and the mule cart nearest on the left, adds dark green tree masses behind the houses, paints the masted boat as twin hulls, rows the sweep boat with side oars, adds a shed full of people on the south bank and a long grassed embankment with a row of houses to the horizon; 1 (draw 2) has the most of the north bank (the passenger boat with its long lattice cabin, the white wall and gateway, the long house, the terrace, the single sweep, the masted boat closed in by two big boats) but invents a herd of a dozen dark mules on the south bank and a stone-coursed bank, doubles the trackers to about ten, and has the deepest ground strip (0.1094: the river reaches the image's bottom edge); 3 (draw 1) puts the eatery and the mule cart nearest, about fifteen trackers or porters in the file, a two-storey terrace hall, and the river running on to far trees and a small tower.
